families.name: P1-F3 — millions-scale token quotes: comparer has no magnitude bridge
families.mechanism: Every one of these values carries unit 'M tokens' in the extraction, with an explicit extractor note invoking instrument v1.2 amendment 6 ('the unit field carries the scale'). The comparer never consumes it. scripts/recompute_c4_claims.py:314-344 implements a percentage bridge only (lines 333-338: `percentish = quoted.is_percentage or (unit or '').strip() == '%'`); there is no short-scale/SI magnitude branch. Result: 785.7 is compared against 770,307,688 and reported as abs_error 770,306,902.3 — a number that says nothing about the document. Decisive control: 071#38[2] ('~47 M') MATCHed because its extraction expression carries the conversion inline (`(a - b) / 1000000`), i.e. the harness handles the scale only when the extractor smuggles it into an arithmetic expression, never when it is declared as a unit on a `read` row. Second failure mode of the same gap: 069#14[1] and 069#14[2] (same figures, verbatim retained as '621.3 M' / '785.7 M') are UNRESOLVED with reason 'unparseable quote' — the parser also lacks magnitude handling. These eight statuses must be treated as uninformative and re-run after the bridge lands; they carry no doc verdict either way.

Ruling 14 demoted the presentation class to advisory and made per-claim era-faithfulness the deciding axis; this document — 50 mismatches that era resolution explains completely — received no era_check at all because 'report.md' has no date in its stem. Un-gate era_check from the presentation class (run it on every mechanical MISMATCH). Additionally consider adding the per-numeral resolution this pass used: find_era_commit resolves the DOCUMENT blob (last-touch), which for a doc edited across ten days attributes numerals to commits that merely rewrote surrounding prose. `git log -S<numeral> -- <doc>` gives the introducing commit cheaply and is what separated P1-F2 from a 31-row false doc-defect finding here.

Adding a README naming those three commits would make every era figure quoted across the corpus browsable without git archaeology — and this partition shows the era figures are what documents actually quote.

escalations.title: The document's cost conclusion reverses under the audited manifests, and its section 9.3 'Suggested paper text' is the vehicle
escalations.detail: Section 9.1 states 'text-HIGH offers the same corrected-F1 ceiling at 2.9x lower API cost ($126.81 vs $364.70), making it the cost-efficient Pareto choice for post-review deployments', and section 9.3 packages the same numbers as verbatim-liftable paper prose. Under the 2026-06-12 audited manifests the ordering INVERTS: image $200.833 is CHEAPER than text-HIGH $207.3382 (by $6.51, 3.1 %), so the ratio is 0.97x, not 2.9x, and the 'text-HIGH is the cost-efficient choice' recommendation is falsified. text-MIN remains the Pareto floor but by a wider margin ($30.44; 6.60x below image, not 6.0x). Verified mechanism, re-derived from the manifests' own declared flex rates: text-HIGH's proposer bill is 200.9315 = 64,142,910 x 0.25/1e6 + (8,238,720 + 115,025,126) x 1.5/1e6, of which the 115.0 M thinking tokens alone are $172.54 (86 %); image's proposer bill is 195.3499 = 47,658,863 uncached x 0.25/1e6 + 621,058,706 cached x 0.05/1e6 + (6,419,778 + 95,168,363) x 1.5/1e6, where the cache saves $124.21 against uncached pricing. The era manifests did not bill thinking at all (binding fact b), which is precisely what hid the reversal. Per the project's Research Finding Calibration rule this needs human judgement before any repair text is drafted: the correct new sentence is a genuinely different claim about modality cost, not a number swap.
escalations.asks: Confirm the direction with the Google billing console if possible — the audit report flags its corrected figures as LOWER BOUNDS (retry spend unmeasured; section 8), and image/text-HIGH are now within 3 % of each other, which is inside that uncertainty. If the console cannot separate them, the honest refreshed claim is 'image and text-HIGH cost approximately the same' rather than a new ordering.

escalations.severity: MEDIUM — procedural, flips 31 of 50 rows in this partition
escalations.title: Era granularity: document-blob era (harness) vs per-numeral authoring era (this pass)
escalations.detail: Ruling 12 specifies re-resolution 'at the source document's era commit', and the harness implements that as the commit whose blob matches the extraction's git_blob — i.e. the document's LAST-TOUCH commit. Ruling 14 then made 'per-claim era-faithfulness' the deciding axis and, for entry-dated registers, moved the snapshot unit from the file to the entry. For a synthesis document edited across ten days these two give opposite answers: at the last-touch commit (95111a3f1) 31 of my 50 rows are wrong, so the whole cost block would be DOC-DEFECT-AT-ERA; at each numeral's introducing commit all 50 are faithful, so it is SNAPSHOT-DIVERGENCE. This pass chose per-numeral, on the evidence that commit 6e813e18e rewrote the surrounding F1 prose without altering a single cost numeral (diff-verified) and that the document self-dates its cost figures per track at line 249. But the choice is not derivable from the rulings as written, and it will recur on every long-lived synthesis document in the corpus.
escalations.asks: Pin the granularity in a ruling: is the era unit (a) the document blob, (b) the line's blame commit, or (c) the numeral's introducing commit via git log -S? Note that (b) is the WORST of the three here — it would have mis-dated 14 of my rows to 6e813e18e purely because an adjacent F1 number changed on the same line. If (c) is adopted, R5's instrument change follows.
